Zeng, Sasselov & Jacobsen 2016 (ApJ 819:127, arXiv:1512.08827) states its relation R/R⊕ = (1.07 − 0.21·CMF)·(M/M⊕)^(1/3.7) is applicable to 1–8 M⊕ and CMF 0.0–0.4 (retrieved and confirmed). At CMF = 1/3 the coefficient is exactly 1.0, so 1–8 M⊕ maps to R ∈ [1.000, 1.754] R⊕ (recomputed: 8^(1/3.7) = 1.754197044080575). At the paper's own best-fit CMF = 0.26 the band is [1.015, 1.781].

The gravity expression at /home/ax/projects/well-dipper/body-condition-vector.js:37 currently applies exponent 1.0, not the Zeng exponent — it is g = g_c·(R/R_c), derived in its own comment from M = M_c·(R/R_c)³. The Zeng-based value (a = 1.70) exists only as a proposal in research/superearth-relief-law-2026-07-28.md:58; grep finds no 1/3.7 anywhere in the gravity path. The correct statement is therefore about the SHAPE of the site, not the current exponent: :37 is a single expression with no composition gate and no radius branch, so whatever exponent it carries — 1.0 today, 1.70 if the brief's fix ships — is applied uniformly across the entire reachable radius domain and to all 18 presets, including icy ones (Titan R_c 0.4, Frozen 0.5, Europa 0.5, Moon/Mercury 0.38) and gas ones (Sub-Neptune 2.7, Neptunian 3.9, Saturnian 9.4, Jovian 11.2, Hot Jupiter 13.0), for which Zeng's rocky two-layer PREM model has no validity at all.

The reachable domain is [0.27, 16] R⊕ (59.3×), not the slider's [0.3, 16] (53.3×): the lab's draw site passes { labUnlock: true } and LAB_UNLOCKED_RANGES['Moon/Mercury (impact-airless)'] is [0.27, 0.38], per the codebase's own corrected note at world-engine-lab.html:5268-5271.

Replace "~97% of the reachable domain would be extrapolation" with the measured value and state the metric: ~95% measured linearly in radius ((1.754−1.000)/(16−0.27) = 4.8% valid), or ~86% measured in slider travel (ln(1.754)/ln(16/0.27) = 13.8% valid) — the latter being the metric the slider is actually built on, since radiusFromT(t) = MIN·(MAX/MIN)^t (planet-lod-lab-core.js:87-95) makes equal travel a constant multiplicative step. Finally, the brief's hedge is not the quoted "rocky planets above 1 Earth radius"; it reads "any Earth-composition planet above 1 R⊕" (:61) with the amplitude law branched "for R > 1" (:83). Separately, the brief mis-cites the file as src/worldengine/base/body-condition-vector.js:37 (:64) — no such path exists; the only copy is at repo root.

refuted.claim: Math.pow(1.0, y) === 1.0 bit-exact for every finite non-NaN y, including 1.70, non-integer y, and y arriving from a variable — this is spec-mandated, not incidental.
refuted.correction: Empirically, Math.pow(1.0, y) and 1.0 ** y return bit-exact 1.0 (0x3FF0000000000000) in V8/node for every finite y tested — 24 targeted values plus 3M random finite double bit patterns, including 1.70, non-integer y, and y from a variable — with NaN only for NaN/±Infinity exponents. But this is NOT spec-mandated for general y. ECMA-262 §6.1.6.1.3 (Number::exponentiate) mandates an exact 1𝔽 for base 1 only when exponent is ±0𝔽 (and mandates NaN when exponent is NaN or ±∞); for every other finite exponent the algorithm falls through to "Return an implementation-approximated Number value representing the result of raising ℝ(base) to the ℝ(exponent) power", and §21.3.2 explicitly allows implementations "some latitude… in the choice of approximation algorithms" for pow outside enumerated boundary cases. So bit-exactness at y=1.7 rests on engine/libm behaviour (C99 pow(+1,y)=1 plus 1.0 being exactly representable), not on the ECMAScript spec — note the spec deliberately diverges from IEEE-754 pow for base 1 with NaN/±∞ exponents, so IEEE's guarantee cannot be imported wholesale. Verified on V8/x86-64 only; other engines, ARM, and GPU/GLSL pow (16-ULP tolerance) were not tested.

refuted.claim: The exponent is EXACTLY 1.7, not approximately, and the coefficient (1.07−0.21·CMF) cancels identically in the ratio form. The brief's phrasing 'constant to 3 decimals over R = 1.0–2.0' is wrong in both directions: within Zeng's fitted power law it is exactly constant everywhere and for every CMF; within the underlying physics it is not constant at all.
refuted.correction:
Within Zeng, Sasselov & Jacobsen 2016 the exponent is exactly 1.7 and the coefficient does cancel — both confirmed. Corrected statement:

"Zeng et al. 2016 publish the exponent literally as 1/3.7 (arXiv:1512.08827, ApJ 819:127), so within that fitted power law dln g/dln R = 3.7 − 2 = 1.7 exactly, at every radius and for every CMF: the coefficient (1.07 − 0.21·CMF) enters g only as the constant factor k^−3.7 and cancels identically from any fixed-CMF radius ratio. Verified numerically: CMF {0, 0.1, 0.325, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0} reproduce g(1.5)/g(1.0) = 1.5^1.7 to within 6.7e-16 (~1.5 ulp), and log-slopes at R = 1–8 return 1.7 to 10 decimals.

The brief's hedge 'constant to 3 decimals over R = 1.0–2.0' is TRUE but unnecessarily weak — it should read 'exactly constant, at every R and CMF, since the exponent is an algebraic consequence of the published 1/3.7.' It is not wrong.

Two real defects in that line, neither of them the hedge: (1) R = 2.0 implies M = 10–13 M⊕ (CMF 0–0.325), outside Zeng's own 1–8 M⊕ validity that the brief cites one line earlier — the window over-extrapolates the fit; (2) the brief omits Zeng's second validity bound, CMF 0.0–0.4.

Separately: exact constancy is a property of the FIT, not of the underlying PREM physics, which should vary (tending toward the incompressible a = 1.0 at low mass). But the paper states no slope-variation or fit-accuracy figure, so 'within the underlying physics it is not constant at all' is UNVERIFIED and should be marked as reasoning, not a retrieved result.

Finally, the cancellation is scoped to the fixed-CMF radius ratio. Absolute gravity is strongly CMF-dependent — g(R=1) = 0.779 / 0.994 / 1.465 for CMF 0 / 0.325 / 0.8 — so every absolute g downstream in the brief carries a CMF assumption that does not cancel."

refuted.claim: Valencia, O'Connell & Sasselov 2006 (arXiv:astro-ph/0511150) is now RETRIEVED, closing the gap flagged at research/superearth-relief-law-2026-07-28.md. It gives the sub-Earth answer directly and it is NOT 1.0: Super-Mercuries scale as R ∝ M^~0.3, implying g ∝ R^1.333.
refuted.correction:
Valencia, O'Connell & Sasselov 2006 (arXiv:astro-ph/0511150, Icarus 181:545) is RETRIEVED and both quoted passages are verbatim-correct, closing the citation gap flagged at research/superearth-relief-law-2026-07-28.md line 45 (line number exact, no drift). But the two conclusions drawn from it must be weakened:

(1) NOT "g ∝ R^1.333" — the correct statement is g ∝ R^1.23–1.34, central value ~1.30. The 1.3333 is computed from the abstract's rounded "~0.3". The paper's actual fits (Table 2, five cases) are β = 0.3058, 0.2991, 0.3000, 0.3032, 0.3094, giving 1/β−2 = 1.2701, 1.3434, 1.3333, 1.2982, 1.2321 (mean 1.295). The Mercury-realistic baseline (Tsurf=440K, CMF=65%) gives 1.2701, not 1.3333. Because d(g_exp)/dβ = −11.1 at β=0.3, no more than two significant figures are defensible: quote g ∝ R^~1.3.

(2) NOT "gives the sub-Earth answer directly" — it gives the sub-Earth-MASS answer for an IRON-RICH family only. Valencia's Super-Mercuries are 1–10 M_Mercury (0.0553–0.5527 M⊕, recomputed correct) with "similar composition to the Earth's but larger core mass fraction"; the only CMFs modelled are 50/65/80%, versus Earth's 32.59% (paper's Figure 3 caption). There is no Earth-composition sub-Earth-mass run in the paper. Extrapolating the 440K CMF series off-grid to CMF=32.59% does yield β≈0.299 → g_exp≈1.34, but that extrapolation is ours, not the paper's — label it an inference FROM Valencia, not a result OF Valencia, exactly as the companion doc relabelled the Kite 2009 route.

(3) State the paper's own framing rather than inverting it. §4 verbatim: "The relationship R ∝ M^β between the total radius and mass for the Super-Mercuries is closer to the expected β = 1/3 if the average density was constant, than for Super-Earths." Since β=1/3 IS g ∝ R^1.0, the honest summary is: below 1 M⊕ the exponent moves substantially TOWARD the constant-density value 1.0 (from ~1.70 at super-Earth masses down to ~1.30) without reaching it. "It is NOT 1.0" is true but reverses the paper's emphasis.

(4) Restore the truncated clause and its caveat: the conclusions sentence ends "...R ∝ M^~0.3 for different core mass fractions and surface temperatures," but §4 qualifies it — "The exponent for the scaling laws does not change considerably except for the case in which the surface temperature is 1500K."

(5) Separate correction to the Super-Earth band from the same paper: Table 1's ten fitted R exponents run 0.263–0.272 (min 0.263), below the abstract's stated 0.267 floor. So the Super-Earth g exponent band is 1.677–1.802, not 1.677–1.745. It still brackets Zeng's exactly-1.700, so that cross-check stands.

(6) Housekeeping: superearth-relief-law-2026-07-28.json already marks this citation "retrieved": true in its reference list while another node still says "NOT RETRIEVED". Reconcile both files when closing the gap.

refuted.claim: Zeng 2016 is explicitly rocky-only (CMF 0.0–0.4, Fe + MgSiO3). Five presets — Jovian, Saturnian, Neptunian, Sub-Neptune, Hot Jupiter — are h2-he and out of domain for ANY of these exponents. For degenerate giants R is nearly independent of M, so a radius-keyed g law is ill-posed there, not merely inaccurate.
refuted.correction:
Zeng, Sasselov & Jacobsen 2016 (ApJ 819:127) is explicitly rocky-only: abstract verbatim "for two-layer rocky planets based on PREM ... It is applicable to 1~8 M-earth and CMF of 0.0~0.4." Its layers are PREM-EXTRAPOLATED core and Mg-silicate mantle, not the pure Fe + MgSiO3 endmembers — the paper names those as the PRIOR models it supersedes (Zeng & Sasselov 2013; Zeng & Seager 2008; Seager et al. 2007).

Exactly five presets carry composition:'h2-he' in driver-presets.js — Jovian, Saturnian, Neptunian, Sub-Neptune, Hot Jupiter — and all five are out of domain for any Zeng-derived exponent. Their radius draws are entirely >= 2.5 R-earth (RADIUS_RANGES_EARTH: 'sub-neptune' [2.5,4.0], 'gas-giant' [6.0,14.0]; Hot Jupiter NAMED_BODY-locked at 13.0), so they sit on the R>1 branch and would silently inherit the rocky exponent: body-condition-vector.js:37 (repo root, NOT src/worldengine/base/) applies g = g_c*(R/R_c) with no composition gate, and bodyFigure.deriveFigureDescriptor consumes it for gas bodies. giant-drivers.js:231-234 back-solves g from a pinned M0, but only for the climate/storm D-slot triple, so it does not shield the other consumers.

CORRECTED on the failure mode, which is NOT uniform across the five. By Chen & Kipping 2017 the Neptunian/Jovian break is at 0.414 M_J ~= 132 M-earth:
- Jovian (317.8 M-earth) and Hot Jupiter (400 M-earth) ARE degenerate (R ~ M^-0.04). There a radius-keyed g law is genuinely ill-posed: inverting gives M ~ R^-25, g ~ R^-27.
- Saturnian (95.2), Neptunian (17.1) and Sub-Neptune (8.2) are all BELOW the break, in the regime R ~ M^0.59. Measured on the presets' own values, dlnR/dlnM = 0.145 (Sat->Jup), 0.50-0.51 (SubN->Nep, Nep->Sat), 0.65 (Jup->HJ). For those three, a radius-keyed g law is inaccurate (wrong exponent, wrong physics) but well-posed and invertible.

# Super-Earth gravity law (`R^1.70`) — build-readiness assessment

**Target:** `/home/ax/projects/well-dipper/body-condition-vector.js:37`
**Date of assessment:** 2026-07-28 · repo state: `npm run verify-golden` → `PASS — canonical-scenario-v1 matches golden 40c18aad, samples: 1200`

---

## 1. Verdict

**NEEDS-FIX.** The exponent change is safe on goldens and cheap on tests (measured: exactly 3 test failures, all legitimate re-pins), but it is **not build-ready** because two things block it:

1. **The proposed edit as written is ungated.** `body-condition-vector.js:37` is a single expression with no composition branch and no radius branch. Zeng, Sasselov & Jacobsen 2016 is a rocky two-layer PREM fit valid over 1–8 M⊕ / CMF 0.0–0.4, which at CMF = 1/3 is **R ∈ [1.000, 1.754] R⊕** (recomputed: `8^(1/3.7) = 1.754197044080575`). The reachable radius domain is **[0.27, 16] R⊕** and includes 5 h2-he gas presets (Jovian 11.2, Hot Jupiter 13.0, Saturnian 9.4, Neptunian 3.9, Sub-Neptune 2.7) and 8 presets with R_c < 1. Shipping `^1.70` unconditionally applies a rocky self-compression law to gas giants and to sub-Earth bodies where the current `^1.0` is closer to correct. **Composition gating and the sub-Earth branch are scoping decisions that must be made before code lands** (§6).

2. **The largest visible gravity consumer does not read this field at all.** `uniforms.uPerturb.value` — the global relief-amplitude uniform — is fed `state.surfaceGravity`, whose sole writer is the *canonical, radius-blind* `u.surfaceGravity`. Changing line 37 moves nothing there. This is a pre-existing wiring defect, but it means the fix as scoped will not produce the visual outcome the brief implies (§3.1). Decide whether to fix it in the same workstream or declare it out of scope, explicitly.

Everything else is green. Goldens hold, byte-identity holds, the test cost is 3 assertions, and the physics arithmetic is correct.

---

## 2. What the change actually is

### Path correction (the brief is wrong)

The research brief `research/superearth-relief-law-2026-07-28.md` cites `src/worldengine/base/body-condition-vector.js:37`. **That path does not exist.**

```
$ ls -la body-condition-vector.js
-rw-r--r-- 1 ax ax 6276 Jul 20 00:12 body-condition-vector.js
```

The only copy is at the **repo root**. The line number 37 is correct. This matters for two reasons: (a) the root file is *not* scanned by `tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js`, and (b) it is *not* covered by `doc-rot`'s `find src -name '*.js'` scan.

### Current expression, verbatim (`body-condition-vector.js:37`)

```js
  surfaceGravity:  (derived?.surfaceGravity ?? bodySurfaceGravity(fp)) * ((radiusEarth ?? fp.radiusEarth ?? 1.0) / (fp.radiusEarth ?? 1.0)),
```

Its justifying comment (`:32–36`) derives the exponent 1.0 from constant density:

> `g = g_c·(R/R_c)` — the normalized-at-canonical ratio form of `M=(ρ/ρ⊕)·R³` per composition class (`M_derived(R) = M_c·(R/R_c)³ ⇒ g = M_derived/R² = g_c·(R/R_c)`)

### Proposed expression

```js
  surfaceGravity:  (derived?.surfaceGravity ?? bodySurfaceGravity(fp)) * Math.pow((radiusEarth ?? fp.radiusEarth ?? 1.0) / (fp.radiusEarth ?? 1.0), 1.70),
```

### The arithmetic (DERIVATION, not calibration)

Zeng+2016: `R/R⊕ = (1.07 − 0.21·CMF)·(M/M⊕)^(1/3.7)` ⇒ `M ∝ R^3.7` ⇒ `g = M/R² ∝ R^(3.7−2) = R^1.70`, **exactly**, at every R and every CMF. The coefficient `(1.07 − 0.21·CMF)` enters `g` only as a multiplicative constant `k^-3.7` and **cancels identically** in the normalized ratio form the code uses. Confirmed numerically: `Math.pow(1.6, 1.7) = 2.223330217241199`; CMF sweep 0→1 reproduces `(R/R_c)^1.7` to ≤ 2e-15.

**Consequence for AC-0:** the fix needs **no CMF / ironFraction plumbing**. `radiusEarth` is already the third argument. But the exponent `1.70` is a new literature constant, not a driver — see §7.

**Calibration status:** this is a **DERIVATION**, not a calibration. Zeng's relation is a fit to interior-structure models anchored on Earth and Solar-System rocky bodies; there is **no measured super-Earth surface gravity and no measured super-Earth topography** anywhere in the chain. The exponent is defensible for R ∈ [1.00, 1.75] R⊕ and is extrapolation everywhere else. Measured over the reachable slider, the valid band is **4.79% linear-in-radius** or **13.77% of slider travel** (`radiusFromT` is a log map, `planet-lod-lab-core.js:94`) — i.e. **~86–95% of the reachable domain is extrapolation**, depending on metric.

## 3. Blast radius

### 3.1 The structural finding first: the visible relief amplitude does NOT read this field

```
world-engine-lab.html:2999   const u = deriveUniforms(DRIVER_PRESETS[driverUI.preset], driverUI.qualityTier);
world-engine-lab.html:3016   state.surfaceGravity = u.surfaceGravity;
world-engine-lab.html:5903   const _RE = state.planetRadiusEarth, _gNow = state.surfaceGravity ?? 1.0;
world-engine-lab.html:5908   uniforms.uPerturb.value = state.perturb * reliefEnvelope(_RE, _gNow);
```

`grep -n "state\.surfaceGravity" world-engine-lab.html` returns exactly three hits: `:3016` (sole writer), `:4261` (disabled GUI readout), `:5903` (this read). And `deriveUniforms` computes gravity from the **canonical** radius:

```
planet-lod-lab-core.js:609-611
  const radiusEarth = d.radiusEarth ?? 1.0;
  const massEarth = d.massEarth ?? 1.0;
```

## 6. The two design questions the physics does NOT settle

These are scoping decisions. They must be made before code lands, because they determine whether the edit is one expression or a branch.

### 6.1 Composition gating — does the rocky exponent apply to the 5 h2-he presets?

**Physics says no.** Zeng is a rocky two-layer PREM fit; giants are outside it in kind, not just in degree.

The gate is already available with zero new plumbing. `body-condition-vector.js:42` already reads the datum:

```js

```

and `src/worldengine/base/e1Regime.js:67` is the canonical terminal:

```js

```

Census (executed): 18 presets; exactly 5 h2-he — `Gas giant (Jovian)` 11.2, `Gas giant (Saturnian)` 9.4, `Ice giant (Neptunian)` 3.9, `Sub-Neptune (hazy)` 2.7, `Hot Jupiter (locked giant)` 13.0.

**Options:**

| option | consequence |
|---|---|
| **(A) Gate on `fp.atmosphere?.composition === 'h2-he'`, leave giants on `^1.0`** | Physically honest about domain. Cost: one branch. Note the blast radius on giants is *already* near-nil (the E5 path back-solves g away; the relief route terminates at `despun()` before any gravity branch), so this is mostly hygiene — but it prevents `deriveFigureDescriptor` computing gas-giant oblateness off a rocky law. |
| **(B) Import `compositionClass` and gate three-way (gas / icy / rocky)** | Single source of truth for the boundary constants (2.5 / 3.9 / `'h2-he'` / C/O > 1). No import cycle: `e1Regime.js` imports only `alea` + `mathutil` and never reads `surfaceGravity`. Also excludes the 4 icy presets (Titan 0.4, Frozen 0.5, Europa 0.5, Crystal 0.8), for which Zeng's rocky EOS has no validity. Cost: one import from `src/worldengine/**` → triggers Rule 15. |
| **(C) Apply `^1.70` unconditionally** | Simplest diff. Applies a rocky self-compression law to bodies whose real `dg/dR` is flat-to-negative. Measured in-repo evidence against it: fitting `dln g/dln R` between preset pairs gives Sub-Neptune→Neptunian **−0.001**, Neptunian→Saturnian **−0.048**, Jovian→Hot Jupiter **−0.456**. **Not recommended.** |

**Refuted framing worth naming:** it is *not* true that "R is nearly independent of M" for all five. By Chen & Kipping 2017 the Neptunian/Jovian break is ~0.414 M_J ≈ 132 M⊕. Jovian (317.8 M⊕) and Hot Jupiter (400 M⊕) are degenerate — there a radius-keyed g law is genuinely **ill-posed**. Saturnian (95.2), Neptunian (17.1) and Sub-Neptune (8.2) sit below the break where R is strongly monotone in M — there the law is merely **wrong-exponent**, not ill-posed.

### 6.2 The sub-Earth domain — what exponent below 1 R⊕?

**The brief's implicit `^1.0` below 1 R⊕ is an over-correction.** `n = 1.0` is the **M → 0 incompressible asymptote**, not the sub-Earth value.

Valencia, O'Connell & Sasselov 2006 (arXiv:astro-ph/0511150, Icarus 181:545) — retrieved. Abstract verbatim: *"The scaling law obtained for the Super-Mercuries is R∝M^∼0.3."* Converting `β = dlnR/dlnM` to `n = 1/β − 2`:

| source | band | β | **n = dln g/dln R** | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Valencia 2006 Super-Earths | 1–10 M⊕ | 0.263–0.272 (Table 1) | **1.677 – 1.802** | brackets Zeng's 1.700 |
| Zeng 2016 | 1–8 M⊕ | 1/3.7 | **1.700** | the proposal |
| Valencia 2006 Super-Mercuries | 0.055–0.553 M⊕ | ~0.30 (Table 2: 0.2991–0.3094) | **~1.23 – 1.34**, central ~1.30 | iron-rich (CMF 50/65/80%), **not Earth composition** |
| incompressible limit | M → 0 | 1/3 | **1.000** | asymptote only |

**Caveat, stated because it matters:** Valencia's Super-Mercury family is explicitly *"similar composition to the Earth's but larger core mass fraction"* — no Earth-composition sub-Earth-mass run exists in that paper. Extrapolating its CMF trend down to Earth's 32.6% gives β ≈ 0.299 → n ≈ 1.34, but that extrapolation is ours, not the paper's. Treat ~1.3 as an **inference from** Valencia, not a **result of** Valencia.

Also note Valencia's own framing (§4): the sub-Earth exponent moves **toward** the constant-density value, it does not reach it. Do not restate this as "it is NOT 1.0" — the honest summary is "it falls from ~1.70 to ~1.30, not to 1.00."

**Options:**

| option | consequence |
|---|---|
| **(A) Piecewise absolute-R with `n_lo = 4/3`, `n_hi = 1.70`, continuous at R=1** | Best physical fidelity of the cheap options. Derivative kink at R=1 (slope jumps 1.333 → 1.700, a 1.275× change) — continuous in g, discontinuous in dg/dR; visible only as a slope change while dragging. Byte-exact at R === R_c. Two `Math.pow`, one branch. |
| **(B) Piecewise with `n_lo = 1.0`** (the brief's implicit form) | Wrong by ~33% in the exponent across the band where 8 of 13 rocky/icy presets live. Not recommended. |
| **(C) Smooth blend**, `ln f(R) = n_lo·lnR + ((n_hi−n_lo)/s)·ln(1+R^s)` | No kink, C^∞, correct asymptotes. Introduces a sharpness parameter `s` that **nothing constrains** — pure taste. Within ~5% of (A) everywhere. |
| **(D) Pure ratio power `^1.70` everywhere** (the brief as literally written) | Correct for exactly 2 presets over part of their range. Wrong for the 8 presets with R_c < 1 at **every** off-canonical radius. At Mars (R_c=0.53): at R=4 it is 56% above the piecewise form; at R=0.27, 38% below. **Fixes super-Earths by breaking Mars, Mercury, Europa and Titan.** Do not ship. |

### 6.3 The ratio-form trap (why 6.2 is not a corner case)

The code is `g = g_c · f(R)/f(R_c)`, an **anchored ratio**. A piecewise-in-absolute-R law and a pure ratio power agree **iff R and R_c sit on the same branch**. Since **8 of 13** rocky/icy presets have R_c < 1 (`Moon/Mercury 0.38, Titan 0.40, Frozen 0.50, Europa 0.50, Mars 0.53, Crystal 0.80, Lava 0.90, Venus 0.95`), those never agree at any off-canonical radius. The remaining 5 diverge across all of R < 1 — which every preset can reach (slider `[0.3, 16]`, `planet-lod-lab-core.js:91-92`) and which is `Carbon (high C/O)`'s **entire** draw band (`'carbon': [0.4, 0.9]`, `src/core/ScaleConstants.js`, despite R_c = 1.1).

If the implementation is piecewise, **that is a second law** and should be registered as such (§7.3), not hidden inside a single-exponent claim.
